data.description:
## Context / Problem
`GerritClient.clone_change_ref` (src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py) builds a fetch URL whose userinfo part holds the bot user and `gerrit_bot_token` and passes it as a positional argument to `git fetch -q --depth 2`. The secret is therefore in the git process's command line for the length of the fetch. On 2026-11-22 at 19:32 PST a read-only `ps` sample on the prod host (taken for ultrashort-emaciated-krill) showed the full URL, password included, in the review-bot's git child. Anyone who can list processes on the host or in the container (`ps`, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, SSM command output, monitoring agents) can read it. The token is the review-bot account's dual-scope Gerrit credential (REST and git).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No review-bot git invocation carries a credential in its argv; the fetch authenticates through a channel that is not in the command line (credential helper, or a header passed through the environment).
- [ ] A test fails if `clone_change_ref` puts the bot token in the git argv.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The review-bot Gerrit token is rotated after the fix deploys, since it has appeared in process listings.
data.title: Review-bot passes its Gerrit HTTP password in git's argv, visible in any process listing
